name: Question 15
problem:
A particle $P$ of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ is subject to the external forces 

$$
{F}_{1}=⟨8\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)⟩,\,{F}_{2}=⟨12-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,10-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)⟩,
$$

where ${F}_{1}$ and ${F}_{2}$ are measured in newtons and $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Given that the velocity of $P$ equals $⟨1,\,-1⟩\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s},$ calculate the speed of $P$ when $t=3\,\text{s}.$ Do not round the answer.

The speed of $P$ when $t=3\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}.$
worked_solution:
Newton's second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

The resultant force $F$ acting on $P$ equals the sum of the forces acting on $P.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F & ={F}_{1}+{F}_{2} \\  & =⟨8\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)⟩+⟨12-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,10-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨12,\,10⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

By Newton's second law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{F}{m} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot ⟨12,\,10⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,\frac{5}{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To compute the velocity vector $v,$ we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\int a\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨3,\,\frac{5}{2}⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 3\,\text{d}t,\,\int \frac{5}{2}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨3t,\,\frac{5}{2}t⟩+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a (vector) constant of integration. 

We can solve for $C$ by substituting $v=⟨1,\,-1⟩\,\text{m/s}$ and $t=0\,\text{s}$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨1,\,-1⟩ & =⟨3(0),\,\frac{5}{2}(0)⟩+C \\ ⟨1,\,-1⟩ & =⟨0,\,0⟩+C \\ C & =⟨1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity of $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨3t,\,\frac{5}{2}t⟩+⟨1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨3t+1,\,\frac{5}{2}t-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=3,$ the velocity equals

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =⟨3(3)+1,\,\frac{5}{2}(3)-1⟩ \\  & =⟨10,\,\frac{13}{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the speed of $P$ when $t=3$ equals the magnitude of $v(3).$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|v(3)| & =\sqrt{{10}^{2}+{(\frac{13}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{569}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of $P$ when $t=3\,\text{s}$ is $\frac{\sqrt{569}}{2}\,\text{m/s}.$

Given that the velocity of P equals ⟨1,−1⟩m/s when t=0s, calculate the speed of P when t=3s. Do not round the answer.

EXPLANATION

Newton's second law states that F=ma, where F is the resultant force, m is the mass, and a is the acceleration.

The resultant force F acting on P equals the sum of the forces acting on P. Therefore,

F=F1+F2=⟨8cos⁡t,4ln⁡(t+1)⟩+⟨12−8cos⁡t,10−4ln⁡(t+1)⟩=⟨12,10⟩.

By Newton's second law, we have

a=Fm=14⋅⟨12,10⟩=⟨3,52⟩.

To compute the velocity vector v, we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

v=∫adt=∫⟨3,52⟩dt=⟨∫3dt,∫52dt⟩=⟨3t,52t⟩+C

where C is a (vector) constant of integration.

We can solve for C by substituting v=⟨1,−1⟩m/s and t=0s into the above, as follows:

⟨1,−1⟩=⟨3(0),52(0)⟩+C⟨1,−1⟩=⟨0,0⟩+CC=⟨1,−1⟩

Therefore, the velocity of P at time t is given by

v=⟨3t,52t⟩+⟨1,−1⟩=⟨3t+1,52t−1⟩.

When t=3, the velocity equals

v(3)=⟨3(3)+1,52(3)−1⟩=⟨10,132⟩.

Finally, the speed of P when t=3 equals the magnitude of v(3). Therefore,

|v(3)|=102+(132)2=5692.

So, the speed of P when t=3s is 5692m/s.
